claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a new assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'm here to help you through the Child Benefit eligibility process. 

To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for. Let me ask you the first key question:

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know if they are:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16-19 years old**
- **20 years old or over**

Also, if you have more than one child, please tell me about each one and their age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh hello, yes I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child, Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's very helpful.

So you have **Alex, who is 8 years old** - that means Alex is under 16, which is great news as this is a key qualifying age for Child Benefit.

Let me continue through the eligibility checks for Alex. The next thing I need to determine is whether Alex is working full-time, as this can affect eligibility.

**Is Alex working full-time (16+ hours per week)?**

Please note: Full-time work typically means working 16 or more hours per week. Since Alex is only 8 years old, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this to complete the assessment properly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That makes sense - Alex is only 8 years old, so no full-time work to worry about. 

Now I need to check a few more important eligibility criteria. Let me navigate to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to ask about Alex's situation regarding paid work:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Given that Alex is 8 years old, I expect this would be "yes" - but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't have any paid work - they're just 8 years old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's confirmed - Alex has no paid work. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check if Alex is receiving certain benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of the following benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(In other words, is Alex not claiming these benefits themselves?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name - they're only 8.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's confirmed - Alex isn't receiving those benefits. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, I expect the answer is no - but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - they're only 8 years old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is definitely not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency situation, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK, or do you have a residency status that qualifies you?**

Here are the main pathways that could qualify you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold, OR
   - You're actively seeking work, OR
   - You have sufficient resources and aren't claiming certain benefits, OR
   - You're studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries**

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's perfect - you normally live in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. There are a few ways you could be considered responsible:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** - You have Alex living with you as your household
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents for Alex (at least the equivalent amount of Child Benefit)
3. **You pay maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that covers Alex's upkeep

Which applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially - I contribute towards things like clothes and school dinners for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Good to know! So you're contributing to Alex's upkeep through financial support for things like clothes and school dinners. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important question about other claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or have they already been awarded Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent currently claiming Child Benefit for them?
- Has anyone else already been awarded Child Benefit for Alex?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's confirmed - no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check where Alex is living:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **In hospital** - Being treated in hospital long-term
- **In care** - In local authority care
- **Fostered** - Living with foster carers
- **Living normally** - Living with family/guardians at home

Which applies to Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally - they're with their other parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally with their other parent. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. Now I need to check one final thing:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council not providing financial support for Alex's housing or upkeep? (This would typically apply if Alex were in care, but since they're living normally with their other parent, the answer should be "yes" - the council is not paying.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex - they're just living with their other parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final check completed. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I now have all the information I need. Let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Great News! You're ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit** ✓

---

### **Your Result:**
**You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### **Why You Qualify:**
You meet all the eligibility requirements:

✓ **Alex's age**: 8 years old (under 16 - qualifying age)
✓ **No full-time work**: Alex is not working
✓ **No disqualifying benefits**: Alex is not claiming ESA or Universal Credit
✓ **No apprenticeship**: Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
✓ **Your residency**: You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
✓ **Your responsibility**: You contribute financially to Alex's upkeep (clothes, school dinners)
✓ **No other claimants**: Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✓ **Living normally**: Alex lives with their other parent, not in hospital, care, or fostered
✓ **Council not paying**: The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide documentation**: Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
4. **Important note about the High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which could reduce or eliminate your benefit
5. **Payment frequency**: Child Benefit is normally paid every 4 weeks, or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits

For more information and to make your claim, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

---

Do you have any other questions about your Child Benefit eligibility or the claiming process?
